identity.name: Dabuyid dynasty
alt_names: Gilan and Tabaristan under the Dabuyids

land.text: Gilan and, by treaty with the Arabs, Tabaristan: the Sasanian Padashwargar country

predecessors.note: A cadet branch of the House of Sasan; Dabuya's titles Gil-i Gilan and Padashwargarshah were given by Yazdegerd III.

successors.note: Infobox 'Succeeded by: Abbasid Caliphate, Bavand dynasty, Baduspanids, Qarinvand dynasty'; the later local dynasties (Bavand, Baduspanids, Qarinvand) are not dated on the page and have no Cliopatria row.

capitals.name: Fuman
capitals.note: Infobox: Fuman (660-760); the page gives no seat for 642-659 and the dot starts at the founding. Farrukhan moved the capital to Sari under his reign (712-728).

capitals.name: Sari
capitals.note: 'He moved his capital there' (Farrukhan page, no year); the Dabuyid infobox still gives Fuman 660-760.

rulers.name: Farrukhan the Great
rulers.note: Modern scholars place his rise in the 670s (Dabuyid page).

rulers.name: Farrukhan the Little
rulers.title: regent for Khurshid
rulers.note: Table: 740/741-747/48; 'for eight years the regency was exercised by his uncle Farrukhan-i Kuchak' (Khurshid page).

rulers.name: Khurshid
rulers.note: Reign 740/741-760 (infobox 759/60) with the regency to 748; died 761 by suicide. Listed from the end of the regency.

correction.text: 642-643: the Cliopatria shape of 644 extended back to the founding

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts in 644, the page in 642 ('a founder of the dynasty in 642'). The 644 shape is extended back two years; whether Tabaristan was already inside in 642 is open (ledger, found event).

64,825 km2: Mazandaran and Gilan with a part of Golestan and of the Talysh coast (Iran and Azerbaijan), about 80% of the Tabaristan region and 82% of Daylam. The page gives no area figure; the infobox territory 'Azerbaijan, Iran, Turkmenistan' and 'Tabaristan and parts of western Khorasan' fit, and Gilan is covered. The Farrukhan page has direct rule only over 'Ruyan and the valleys of Tabaristan as far as Tammisha', Gilan and Daylam 'ruled only in name' and Gurgan under a marzban, so the shape is generous on the east and the lowlands.
64,800 km2 for 647-717, the same shape. Dabuya and Farrukhan the Great hold Tabaristan with the mountains and Gilan nominally; the shape stands as a soft frontier.

64,405 km2 for 718-749. The Tabaristan page: Dadhburzmihr (r. 720-740) 'may have temporarily lost control of Tabaristan to the Arabs, as indicated by his lack of coinage' and Khurshid 'managed to safeguard his realm against the Umayyads'; nothing dated, so the shape stands.
64,138 km2 for 750 alone: Khurshid 'was forced to submit to the Abbasid armies under Abu Muslim' during the revolution (undated), with no change of border on the page.
64,405 km2 for 751-754: after Abu Muslim's murder in 755 Khurshid backed Sunbadh's revolt; before it al-Mansur's pressure raised the tribute. No border change on the page.
Cliopatria ends the Dabuyids in 756, but the Abbasid conquest is 759-760 (al-Tak 'besieged in 759-760') and Khurshid lived to 761 in Daylam. The shape holds through 760; see the next keyframe.

correction.text: 757-760: the 755 shape, until the fall of al-Tak in 760

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 757-760, the Cliopatria gap. The dynasty ends in 760 with the Abbasid conquest (Dabuyid infobox 'to the Abbasid conquest in 760').

region.text: Gilan, with control of Tabaristan by the treaty with the Arabs

ledger.note: 642: Gil Gavbara founds the Dabuyid dynasty in Gilan. 'Piruz died around 642 and was succeeded by Gil Gavbara as the ruler of Gilan'; he is 'a founder of the dynasty in 642, ruling until his death in 660'; he 'signed a peace treaty with the Arab conquerors' and 'was given control of Tabaristan' (no year). The Tabaristan page has him 'conquered all of Daylam and Gilan and planned on extending his conquests to Tabaristan'; the Farrukhan page says the traditional account has the family autonomous 'in the 640s' while Pourshariati puts Farrukhan's establishment of its rule 'sometime in the 670s'. Tabaristan's entry date is therefore not settled.
660: Fuman is the capital. Infobox: 'Fuman (660-760)'; Gil Gavbara died in 660 and his son Dabuya succeeded him. The Gil Gavbara page is silent on his seat.

Year not on the page: Farrukhan the Great (712-728) founded Sari and 'he moved his capital there', with a palace at Shahr-e Espahbodan between Sari and Amol. 712 is the start of his reign, my bridging; the Dabuyid infobox keeps Fuman to 760.

region.text: Tabaristan and Gurgan, invaded by the Arab governor Yazid ibn al-Muhallab

ledger.note: 716: 'In 716, the Arab governor of Iraq and Khurasan, Yazid ibn al-Muhallab invaded Tabaristan with the intent to conquer it.' He initially defeated Farrukhan, 'seizing Dihistan and Gurgan'; Farrukhan then recruited Daylamites and Gilites and incited Gurgan to revolt and 'The Arab garrison was subsequently massacred'.

717: Yazid withdraws. He made a treaty agreeing to withdraw 'in return for tribute' and 'The following year (717), the caliph Umar II (r. 717-720) had Yazid dismissed and imprisoned'. The Dabuyids 'owed only the payment tribute and nominal vassalage to the Muslim caliphate'; the amount and the dates of other payments are not on the page.

region.text: Tabaristan, invaded by the Abbasid generals Abu al-Khasib Marzuq and Khazim bin Khuzaymah

ledger.note: 759: al-Mansur's campaign. He sent Abu al-Khasib Marzuq and Khazim bin Khuzaymah 'with the intention of completely subduing the country and making it a province'; Khurshid fled to the fortress of al-Tak, 'besieged in 759-760'. Al-Mansur's pressure had earlier raised the tribute 'to the level paid to the Sassanids' (undated).

region.text: Tabaristan, made an Abbasid province under Marzuq

ledger.note: 760: al-Tak falls and Khurshid's family is taken to Baghdad; the Tabaristan page: Khurshid 'was defeated in 760 by Abbasid general Abu al-Khasib Marzuq', the first Abbasid governor, who built the great mosque in Sari. Khurshid escaped to Daylam and in 760 invaded Tabaristan from there and was repulsed.
760: the Abbasid conquest of Tabaristan ends with the fall of al-Tak and Khurshid's repulse.

region.text: the Dabuyid realm at its fall

ledger.note: 760: the Dabuyid dynasty ends. Its rule 'lasted from around 642 to the Abbasid conquest in 760'; Khurshid 'took poison, probably in 761' (Khurshid page) and the Dabuyid page says 'when the king was captured in 761, his family committed suicide', a disagreement it does not reconcile; his coins were struck until 764.

wars.name: Yazid ibn al-Muhallab's invasion of Tabaristan

zones.text: Gurgan and Dihistan, seized and lost

wars.outcome: Dabuyid victory: Farrukhan the Great contained the invasion; Yazid withdrew 'in return for tribute' and was dismissed in 717.
wars.note: The Tabaristan page also dates it 716; the Umayyad Caliphate page has 'Yazid ibn al-Muhallab attempted to conquer Jurjan and Tabaristan'.

wars.name: Abbasid conquest of Tabaristan

zones.text: Tabaristan and the fortress of al-Tak

wars.outcome: Abbasid victory: Tabaristan became an Abbasid province under Marzuq; Khurshid fled to Daylam and died in 761.
wars.note: Dated 759-760 on the Khurshid page; the Dabuyid page has the king captured in 761.

certainty.note: Mountain and forest frontiers of Tabaristan and Gilan; Gurgan, Daylam and the Talysh coast are the soft edges (marzban rule, nominal rule). No treaty line on any page.

notes:
Written for group me-07 on 2026-10-19 from five pages (budget 5). The pages for the Arab conquest of Tabaristan (651 treaty, 673-676 campaigns) are silent in the Tabaristan article; the Persia article (opened for the Rashidun dossier, not listed here) dates a peace treaty of 'the ruler of Tabaristan' to 651 without naming him.
Cliopatria: the row 644-756 starts two years after the page (642) and ends four years before it (760); added as the 642 and 757 keyframes. The shape (64.8 k km2) was measured against the gazetteer: it covers Gilan fully and Mazandaran, with part of Golestan and Ardabil/Talysh; the Farrukhan page excludes Gurgan. Not on the pages: the Tang embassy of 746, where Khurshid is recognised as a vassal prince 'king Hu-lu-ban' (Khurshid page) - a vassal event for the Tang dossier if the East Asia group wants it; Khurshid's rebellion against Marwan II in the Third Fitna (744-750); Abu Muslim's submission (undated); the tribute amount; the region of Dihistan and Qumis.
Dadhburzmihr's years differ between the Dabuyid table (728-740/741) and the Tabaristan page (720-740); the first is used. Khurshid: reign to 760 (table) or 759/60 (infobox); death 761 by poison (Khurshid page) or by suicide with his family on capture (Dabuyid page).
